steps.text: Long before clocks, people measured time in clever ways. Let's travel through the history of timekeeping.
Tap a device to explore it — try the sundial, then the water clock.
Sundials used the Sun's shadow; water clocks and sand timers used steady flow; later came pendulum clocks, and today, quartz and digital clocks.
Each new device measured time more accurately than the last. All of them rely on something that repeats at a steady, regular rate.

coach.mission: Explore how people measured time through history.
whenStuck: Tap each timekeeping device to see how it works.
Notice what repeats steadily in each one.
whenWrong: Every timekeeper uses something regular and repeating — a shadow, a flow, a swing.
Newer devices simply measure time more accurately.
whenCorrect: Right — that device measured time in its own clever way.
Good — all clocks rely on a steady, repeating action.
coach.done: You've seen how timekeeping improved over history. Explore more, or move on when you're ready.
